topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and frames the study of complement within the immunology course.

topics.label: Foundational concepts and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature rules, and core biochemical activation of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three upstream pathways that recognise pathogens and trigger surface-bound C3 convertase activity.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream immune outcomes triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the diverse clinical presentations and disease phenotypes that arise from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the mechanisms evolved by pathogens to resist complement destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
